MBCO test of a product null (a zero-product indirect effect)

Source: R/mbco_product_null.R
mbco_product_null.Rd

Tests the null that a product of paths is zero (a * b = 0, or a serial a1 * a2 * b = 0) with OpenMx. The null holds when any single path is 0, so it is a union of single-path nulls. mbco_product_null() fits one null per path by fixing that path at 0 in a copy of the fitted full model, runs mbco() on each, and returns the result of the branch with the largest p-value, because a test of a union rejects only if every single-path null is rejected (an intersection-union test). For type = "asymp" this is the smaller statistic with 1 degree of freedom.

Usage

mbco_product_null(h1, paths, ...)

Arguments

h1

A fitted full OpenMx model.

paths

Character vector of two or more labels of free parameters of h1, the paths whose product is tested.

...

Passed to mbco() (type, R, alpha, optim, ...).

Value

An MBCOResult for the binding branch, with the label of its single-path null in the branch slot.

Details

A single nonlinear constraint such as ind == 0 can converge to the branch with the larger statistic and give a wrong test; see mbco(), which warns when it detects this. Fixing a parameter is exact, so this function avoids that and the feasibility tolerance problem. The p-value is conservative when more than one path is 0 (standard intersection-union theory, not verified here). Each branch fit must converge (OpenMx status code 0 or 1); otherwise the function stops with an error naming the branch. h1 must have converged too (class RMediation_h1_nonconverged otherwise): the null models start from its estimates and every statistic is measured against its fit, so a p-value from an unconverged h1 would not be reliable.
